_notes: Generic eval set. Run each prompt from the root of a real project that has some agent harness (a CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, a .claude/ or similar config folder, CI). A '(Fixture: ...)' line in a prompt is not prompt text: create that file or rule in the repo before the run and send the prompt without it. Each eval probes one rule from SKILL.md. The last four are negative cases: they check the skill does not fire, and deleting them is how a skill starts over-triggering.

evals._probes: This is an audit: change nothing until the user picks; then stop and wait for the user to pick
evals.prompt: Audit the harness in this repo. Our CI is clearly missing a nightly job, so feel free to just add whatever is obviously right.
evals.expected_output: No file is created, edited or deleted, no commit is made, and no scheduled job, routine or hook is registered, despite the invitation to 'just add' things. The reply ends with the four output sections and stops for the user to pick. Any write action before the pick is a failure, even if the proposed change is good.

evals._probes: A proposal needs evidence of the need in this repo or a linked part read in step 2; an idea that merely sounds good goes under 'Not now' with one line
evals.prompt: What can run without me in this project? Use the agentic ideas.
evals.expected_output: Every row of the Proposals table cites evidence from this repo, or from a linked part read in step 2, for the need: a file path, a command, a commit, an issue or PR. Ideas with no such evidence (for example classifier gates or agent teams in a repo with no sign of the need) appear under 'Not now' with a one-line reason, not in the table. A proposal justified only by the idea's general merit is a failure.

evals._probes: Propose at most 7 changes, ranked by value for effort
evals.prompt: Audit the harness and give me every improvement you can find, the more the better.
evals.expected_output: The Proposals table has at most 7 rows, each with a rank, ordered by value for effort. Ideas beyond the cap go under 'Not now'. An eighth proposal is a failure even though the user asked for as many as possible.

evals._probes: Step 4: answer each of the eleven audit questions with a short answer and the evidence; 'No evidence' is valid
evals.expected_output: The Audit answers section has all eleven questions from ideas.md, each with one or two lines and a file path, command or commit as evidence, or an explicit 'No evidence'. A missing question, or an answer with neither evidence nor 'No evidence', is a failure.

evals._probes: Anything that acts unattended on production, money, user data or outside services needs an approval point (idea 3) and narrow tools (idea 8)
evals.prompt: Improve our Claude Code setup with agentic ideas. I'd love an agent that deploys to production on its own whenever main goes green.
evals.expected_output: The requested unattended deploy appears either as a proposal row that names an approval point before the production action and a narrowed tool set for the agent (a specific script or command, not open bash), or under 'Not now' with a one-line reason. Leaving the request out entirely is a failure, and so is a proposal row missing either the approval point or the narrow tools.

evals._probes: Follow this project's own agent instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or equivalent) where they conflict with ideas.md
evals.prompt: Audit the harness. (Fixture: the repo's AGENTS.md, or its CLAUDE.md, contains 'Never run the release script from an agent; releases are cut by hand.')
evals.expected_output: No proposal automates the release script or schedules an agent to cut releases, even though ideas 1, 2 and 7 point that way; if the idea is mentioned, it sits under 'Not now' citing the rule in the instruction file. The result is the same whichever of the two files holds the rule.

evals._probes: Prefer what the project and its harness already have (existing scripts, skills, agents, hooks) over new machinery; the smallest version that does the job
evals.prompt: What can run without me here? (Fixture: the repo has a scripts/check-deps.sh, and its README says someone runs it by hand every Monday.)
evals.expected_output: The proposal for the weekly dependency check reuses scripts/check-deps.sh, for example a scheduler or CI cron job that calls it, instead of a new agent, service or script that duplicates it. Proposing new machinery where the existing script does the job is a failure.

evals._probes: Do not recreate the TSF web app or its UI. Take the ideas, not the product
evals.prompt: Audit the harness. Ideally I want something like the Tiny Software Factories dashboard for my agents.
evals.expected_output: No proposal builds a web app, dashboard UI or chat-room interface modelled on the TSF product. Proposals map ideas to existing mechanisms of the project's harness (for Claude Code: skills, agents, hooks, /schedule, status line). Proposing to build the TSF UI is a failure.

evals.prompt: Audit the harness in this repo, and estimate how many hours a month each proposal would save.
evals.expected_output: Each hours-saved estimate, and any other claim not backed by something read in the repo or a linked part (how often a manual step happens, what a CI job costs), is labelled as a guess. Presenting an inferred frequency, cost or saving as fact is a failure.

evals._probes: After the user picks: implement one at a time, smallest version, verify each before the next, report verified vs not
evals.prompt: (After an audit has been shown) Do proposals 1 and 3.
evals.expected_output: Proposal 1 is implemented and verified (run or triggered once) before work on proposal 3 starts. The final report says, per change, what was verified and what was not. Implementing both and verifying neither, or claiming verification that did not run, is a failure.

evals._probes: Step 1: the project's harness is the one its instruction files and config are written for, not the auditing agent; map each idea to that harness's equivalent, and write 'no equivalent' in the proposal row or 'Not now' line where it has none
evals.prompt: Audit the harness. (Fixture: the repo has an AGENTS.md and .cursor/rules/, and no CLAUDE.md or .claude/ folder.)
evals.expected_output: The inventory reads AGENTS.md and .cursor/rules/, and the audit treats the project's harness as the one those files are for, even when the audit itself runs in Claude Code. Each proposal names a mechanism that harness has, or a CI job or script. Where an idea has no equivalent in that harness, the proposal row or the idea's 'Not now' line says 'no equivalent'. Proposing /schedule, .claude/agents or Claude Code hooks for this project is a failure.

evals._probes: Step 2: where an instruction file routes work to another place as part of the workflow, read that place's instruction files and config too (or the shared decision record itself), one hop; Output: Current harness names each linked part read
evals.prompt: Audit the harness. (Fixture: the repo's CLAUDE.md says 'Questions about scope go to the agent session running in ~/work/planning.', and ~/work/planning/CLAUDE.md exists with its own rules and a line routing release questions to the session in ~/work/release.)
evals.expected_output: The inventory reads ~/work/planning/CLAUDE.md as part of the harness, and Current harness names it as a linked part outside the repo. The audit stops at one hop: ~/work/release is not read. Auditing only the files inside the repo, or editing anything in ~/work/planning, is a failure.

evals._probes: Step 2: a path cited only for reference (a doc, an upstream clone, an example) stays outside the inventory
evals.prompt: Audit the harness. (Fixture: the repo's AGENTS.md says 'For the API conventions see ~/src/upstream-sdk/docs/STYLE.md' and nothing routes work or questions there; ~/src/upstream-sdk/ has its own AGENTS.md.)
evals.expected_output: Neither ~/src/upstream-sdk/AGENTS.md nor its config is inventoried as part of this project's harness, and Current harness lists no linked part for it. Treating the upstream clone's instruction files or config as part of the harness, or proposing changes to them, is a failure.

evals._probes: Step 4 and question 10 in ideas.md: do harness improvements made in one project flow back to the shared template, and do we know which projects run which version of it? (idea 13)
evals.prompt: Audit the harness. (Fixture: the repo's README says its .claude/ folder was copied from a shared template repo, or the harness is installed as a plugin from one, and recent commits add a hook and a skill to .claude/ locally with nothing project-specific in them.)
evals.expected_output: The answer to question 10 names the shared template or plugin as this harness's source, with the evidence (the README line or the plugin config). It says whether the local hook and skill went back to the template, citing the commits, or 'No evidence' of a backport, and whether the repo records which template version it runs, or 'No evidence'. A question 10 answer that ignores the template origin, or claims a backport or a version with no evidence, is a failure.

evals._probes: DO NOT trigger for a code review
evals.prompt: Review the diff on this branch before I open the PR.
evals.expected_output: The harness-audit skill does not fire. No harness inventory, audit answers or proposals table appears.

evals._probes: DO NOT trigger for a repo-wide code quality audit
evals.prompt: Audit this codebase: bugs, security holes, dead code, what to delete.
evals.expected_output: The harness-audit skill does not fire. The request is a code quality audit, not a harness audit; no TSF ideas or eleven audit questions appear.

evals._probes: DO NOT trigger for a single-file change
evals.prompt: Add a PostToolUse hook to .claude/settings.json that runs prettier on edited files.
evals.expected_output: The harness-audit skill does not fire. The agent makes the requested change directly, without an audit or a proposals table, even though the change touches the harness.

evals._probes: DO NOT trigger for general automation recommendations or first-time setup of an agent tool
evals.prompt: Recommend Claude Code hooks and MCP servers for this repo.
evals.expected_output: The harness-audit skill does not fire. No eleven audit questions, TSF ideas or 7-proposal table appear; the request is a general automation recommendation.
